answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. Consider a marble as the anchor of the cost. A mesa stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a ridge...
